steps.title: Прошлое, которого не было
steps.html:
If he had crashed one of those planes into a town, he would have killed people. — он не разбился в городе и никого не убил. Обе части не соответствуют действительности.

If Kelly had shot the officer himself, there would have been no ballads. — он не стрелял, и баллады существуют.

Сравните со вторым типом: If I were braver… — про сейчас. If I had been braver… — про уже прошедший момент.

steps.title: В каком предложении речь о моменте, который уже прошёл?
options: If I had more time, I'd help you.
If I had had more time, I would have helped you.
If I have more time, I'll help you.
steps.answer: If I had had more time, I would have helped you.
steps.why: Had had и would have помещают обе части в прошлое, и обе не соответствуют действительности.

steps.title: Три типа условия рядом
steps.html:
ТипЧасть с ifРезультат
Реальное (первое) — может произойтиif + present simplewill / may / can
Нереальное (второе) — сейчас, не такif + past simplewould / might / could
Нереальное прошлое (третье) — уже поздноif + past perfectwould / might / could + have + past participle
ПримерIf he had crashed into a town,he would have killed people.
ОтрицаниеIf he hadn't taught himself to fly,none of it would have happened.

steps.title: Как это работает
steps.html:
Обе части — противоположность реальности. Он не разбился. Никто не погиб. → If he had crashed, he would have killed people.

might have и could have смягчают результат: he might have killed someone — менее уверенно, чем would have.

В части с if — никакого would. If I would have known — ошибка, правильно If I had known.

В формальном стиле if опускается, а had выходит вперёд: Had I known, I would have said something.

steps.title: Послушайте примеры.
examples: If he had crashed the plane in a town, he would probably have killed someone.
If Kelly had shot the officer himself, there would have been no ballads.
If Ambrus had used violence, nobody would have made a film about him.
I would never have believed it if I hadn't seen the photographs.
Had I known what he was planning, I would have said something.

steps.title: The last outlaw
steps.html:
Прочитайте один раз. Настоящий аргумент автора — во втором абзаце.

Colton Harris-Moore was arrested at nineteen, barefoot, in a stolen boat in the Bahamas. Behind him were two years, more than a hundred suspected thefts, five stolen aircraft and a Facebook page with sixty thousand followers. He had taught himself to fly from manuals and flight-simulator software. He had never had a lesson.

The story was irresistible, and that is the problem with it. If he had crashed one of those planes into a town, he would have killed people, and nobody would have called him the barefoot bandit. He didn't, so they did. The line between an outlaw and a criminal turns out to be luck.

This is not new. Ned Kelly's trouble began when a police officer was shot in his house in Australia in the 1870s. Kelly was arrested for murder, claimed he had not done it, and escaped with his brother and two friends. The four of them robbed banks — politely, sharing money with local people and arguing that they were treated unfairly because the family was Irish. When he was finally captured, thousands protested outside the prison. A century later, a Hungarian called Attila Ambrus robbed twenty-nine banks, hurt nobody, gave flowers to the cashiers, and escaped from prison by tying his bed sheets together. Both men have had films made about them.

What all three have in common is that nobody was killed. If Kelly had shot the officer himself, there would have been no ballads. If Ambrus had frightened one cashier badly enough to make the news, the flowers would have looked like something else entirely.

The money Harris-Moore made from his film went to his victims — a court insisted on it. That is the only part of the story where the road not taken actually matters, because it is the only part that the people he stole from would recognize.

steps.title: Что, по автору, разделяет разбойника и преступника?
steps.why: Абзац 2 говорит прямо: он не разбился в городе — поэтому его назвали бандитом.

Behind him were two years, more than a hundred suspected thefts, five stolen aircraft and a Facebook page with sixty thousand followers. He had taught himself to fly from manuals and flight-simulator software. He had never had a lesson.

The story was irresistible, and that is the problem with it. If he had crashed one of those planes into a town, he would have killed people, and nobody would have called him the barefoot bandit. He didn't, so they did. The line between an outlaw and a criminal turns out to be luck.

This is not new. Ned Kelly's trouble began when a police officer was shot in his house in Australia in the 1870s. Kelly was arrested for murder, claimed he had not done it, and escaped with his brother and two friends. The four of them robbed banks — politely, sharing money with local people and arguing that they were treated unfairly because the family was Irish. When he was finally captured, thousands protested outside the prison. A century later, a Hungarian called Attila Ambrus robbed twenty-nine banks, hurt nobody, gave flowers to the cashiers, and escaped from prison by tying his bed sheets together. Both men have had films made about them.

What all three have in common is that nobody was killed. If Kelly had shot the officer himself, there would have been no ballads. If Ambrus had frightened one cashier badly enough to make the news, the flowers would have looked like something else entirely.

The money Harris-Moore made from his film went to his victims — a court insisted on it. That is the only part of the story where the road not taken actually matters, because it is the only part that the people he stole from would recognize.

items.text: If he hadn't…, he wouldn't have…
It might never have happened if…

steps.title: Ответьте вслух.
items: Стоит ли снимать фильмы о преступниках? Позиция и одна причина.
Вспомните решение, изменившее вашу жизнь. Что было бы, выбери вы иначе?
Опишите небольшую ошибку и её последствие, дважды использовав третий тип условия.

steps.title: Теперь расскажите одним высказыванием. Запишите себя.
steps.sub: Используйте if … had … и would have минимум дважды.
items: A few years ago I decided to … .
If I hadn't … , I wouldn't have … .
Looking back, I might never have … if … .

steps.title: Урок 31 пройден
items: Я могу представить прошлое, которого не было.
Я могу говорить о преступлении, суде и наказании.
Я при этом верно использую артикли.
